articles.title: Scottish Football Podcast - Edinburgh Divided: Hearts' Momentum and Hibs' Challenge - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: The contrasting stories of Hearts and Hibs, plus a big night for the Scotland WNT.
articles.body:
Radio Scotland , · 13 Oct 2026 , · 28 mins

Hearts have emerged as one of the Premiership's early success stories, while city rivals Hibs continue their search for consistency under new manager Marink Reedijk. Andy Burke is joined by Hibs Women's boss Joelle Murray and Scotsman sports editor Mark Atkinson to assess the contrasting fortunes of Edinburgh's two biggest clubs, the impact of Hearts' ambitious recruitment strategy and the challenges facing Easter Road. articles.title: Chanceler do Vaticano diz estar 'preocupado' com cirurgia de Leão XIV | G1
articles.standfirst: Cardeal Parolin afirmou que pontífice 'é exemplo de serenidade'. Leão XIV será submetido a cirurgia nesta terça (13) para retirada de nódulo em seu pulmão. Vaticano não informou nem se nódulo é benigno ou maligno, mas que era 'bem localizado e controlado'.
articles.summary: Cardeal Parolin afirmou que pontífice 'é exemplo de serenidade'. Leão XIV será submetido a cirurgia nesta terça (13) para retirada de nódulo em seu pulmão. Vaticano não informou nem se nódulo é benigno ou maligno, mas que era 'bem localizado e controlado'.
articles.body:
O secretário de Estado do Vaticano , o cardeal Piero Parolin, afirmou nesta terça-feira (13) que está "preocupado" com a cirurgia do papa Leão XIV "porque não se esperava uma coisa dessas", mas que o pontífice está "sereno".

Em entrevista à imprensa italiana na manhã, Parolin falou sobre o susto que o nódulo descoberto no pulmão do papa causou no Vaticano, mas ele assegurou se tratar de "um raio em céu azul", em alusão à saúde de Leão XIV —que faz natação e joga tênis.

Parolin disse que conversou com Leão XIV sobre a cirurgia ontem à tarde, quando expressou sua solidariedade. “Conversamos com muita serenidade. O Santo Padre é realmente um grande exemplo nesse sentido. (...) Todos ficamos impressionados”, afirmou.

O papa Leão XIV foi internado na manhã desta terça no hospital Gemelli, de Roma , para uma operação de retirada de nódulo. O Vaticano não afirmou se o nódulo é maligno ou benigno, mas que está "bem controlado e em estágio inicial". Sua cirurgia estava estava agendada para ocorrer às 11h no horário de Brasília , segundo informaram fontes da Santa Sé à repórter Mirticeli Medeiros.

➡️ Um nódulo pulmonar é uma massa densa encontrada no pulmão. Pesquisas sugerem que a maioria dos nódulos detectados em exames de rotina e sem estar associados a sintomas, costuma ser benigna . Nem o Vaticano, nem o papa informaram a natureza do nódulo.

O pontífice, de 71 anos, não tem nenhum outro problema de saúde conhecido.

O papa Leão XIV cumprimenta o médico Andrea Cambieri ao chegar ao hospital Gemelli para uma cirurgia de retirada de um nódulo no pulmão, em 13 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Guglielmo Mangiapane/ Reuters

No domingo (11), o pontífice surpreendeu fiéis ao anunciar , durante uma oração na Praça de São Pedro, no Vaticano, que médicos detectarem um nódulo em seu pulmão "em estágio inicial" .

Leão XIV afirmou que o nódulo foi detectado em estágio inicial e seu crescimento está "bem controlado" . Ainda assim, afirmou o papa, médicos recomendaram a cirurgia para a remoção .

“Queridos amigos, durante alguns exames médicos recentes, os médicos encontraram um nódulo localizado em meu pulmão. Ele foi detectado em um estágio muito inicial e está bem localizado. Os médicos consideram a cirurgia adequada. Seguindo a orientação deles, decidi, portanto, submeter-me a uma operação para removê-lo. A cirurgia já está agendada para os próximos dias. Agradeço pela proximidade espiritual de vocês e confio-me às suas orações", disse o papa aos fiéis.

O porta-voz do Vaticano, Matteo Bruni, não deu detalhes do exame , mas afirmou que recuperação do pontífice após a cirurgia deverá levar cerca de uma semana. Por isso, na segunda-feira o papa cancelou toda a sua agenda de atividades até 20 de outubro .

Durante o período de internação, Leão XIV deverá continuar trabalhando a partir do hospital, como já ocorreu com outros pontífices.

O anúncio da cirurgia suscitou questionamentos sobre se Leão XIV, que é dos Estados Unidos mas viveu 20 anos no Peru, manterá a viagem que tem programada para a América Latina. A visita, que inclui passagens por Peru, Uruguai e Argentina, está prevista para ocorrer no início de novembro e durará quase duas semanas.

O Vaticano não informou se a viagem está mantida ou será cancelada. No entanto, na oração no domingo na qual o pontífice fez o anúncio, ele fez referência à viagem, agradecendo a fiéis por orações "pela viagem pastoral que eu farei" .

Também não havia informações, até a última atualização desta reportagem, sobre o atual estado do pontífice , que tem 71 anos e não apresenta nenhum outro problema de saúde conhecido. Ele costuma se exercitar durante a semana, segundo o Vaticano. O pontífice faz natação e joga tênis .

👉 De origem norte-americana, Robert Prevost foi eleito papa em maio de 2025, substituindo o papa Francisco, argentino, que morreu em abril do ano passado após uma série de problemas de saúde.

Papa Leão XIV durante oração dominical — Foto: Filippo Monteforte / AFP

articles.title: Papa Leão XIV: Basílica de Aparecida pede orações por cirurgia | G1
articles.standfirst: Padre Ferdinando Mancilio fez a prece durante celebração no Santuário Nacional, nesta terça-feira (13). A cirurgia do papa para retirada de nódulo está prevista para às 11h, no horário de Brasília.
articles.summary: Papa Leão XIV passa por cirurgia para retirar nódulo no pulmão nesta terça-feira; Santuário de Aparecida realizou prece especial pela saúde do pontífice.
articles.body:
Fiéis que participavam de uma missa no Santuário Nacional de Aparecida , no interior de São Paulo, foram convidados a rezar pela saúde do papa Leão XIV nesta terça-feira (13), data em que o pontífice passará por uma cirurgia para retirar um nódulo no pulmão , em Roma , na Itália.

A prece foi feita pelo padre Ferdinando Mancilio, prefeito da Igreja do Santuário Nacional, durante a celebração das 6h45, na Basílica. Na oração eucarística, ele pediu pela saúde do pontífice e mencionou o procedimento cirúrgico.

“Que a Igreja cresça na caridade, em comunhão com o Papa Leão. Rezemos pela sua saúde. A esta hora, pela diferença de horário, certamente já está internado para a necessária cirurgia pela qual irá passar”, disse o padre na missa.

A cirurgia está prevista para ser realizada às 11h desta terça-feira, no horário de Brasília. Segundo informações divulgadas sobre o procedimento, um boletim médico deve ser emitido às 15h.

Missa na Basílica de Aparecida pede orações pela saúde do papa Leão XIV durante cirurgia — Foto: Foto 1: Reprodução/A12 | Foto 2: Gregorio Borgia/AP

Leão XIV, de 71 anos, foi internado nesta terça-feira em um hospital de Roma para passar por uma operação de retirada de um nódulo no pulmão. O pontífice anunciou no último domingo (11) que médicos haviam identificado a lesão em estágio inicial.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, o Vaticano não havia informado se o nódulo é benigno ou maligno. A previsão é que a recuperação do papa após a cirurgia leve cerca de uma semana.

O papa também tem uma viagem pastoral prevista para novembro, com visitas ao Peru, Uruguai e Argentina. O Vaticano ainda não havia informado se o procedimento afetaria os planos da viagem.

O papa Leão XIV cumprimenta o médico Andrea Cambieri ao chegar ao hospital Gemelli para uma cirurgia de retirada de um nódulo no pulmão, em 13 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Guglielmo Mangiapane/ Reuters

articles.title: Campo Grande amplia tapa-buracos para até 3 mil reparos por dia | G1
articles.standfirst: Número de frentes de trabalho passou de duas para 12 desde junho, e capacidade de reparos pode chegar a 3 mil por dia. Contratos com cinco empresas somam R$ 46,3 milhões.
articles.summary: Número de frentes de trabalho passou de duas para 12 desde junho, e capacidade de reparos pode chegar a 3 mil por dia. Contratos com cinco empresas somam R$ 46,3 milhões.
articles.body:
Campo Grande passou de duas para 12 frentes de tapa-buracos desde junho — Foto: PMCG

Campo Grande passou de duas para 12 frentes de tapa-buracos desde junho. Com o reforço, a capacidade de reparos nas ruas subiu de 1,6 mil para até 3 mil por dia, segundo a prefeitura.

A ampliação ocorreu após o credenciamento de cinco empresas pelo Consórcio Intermunicipal de Desenvolvimento Sustentável da Região Central de Mato Grosso do Sul. Os contratos somam R$ 46,3 milhões e têm duração de um ano.

As equipes atuam em diferentes regiões da Capital, mas a quantidade de frentes de trabalho não significa que todos os buracos das ruas serão resolvidos de imediato. O cronograma é definido pela Secretaria Municipal de Infraestrutura e Serviços Públicos (Sisep), conforme a necessidade de cada via.

Veja os bairros com serviços de tapa-buracos

De acordo com a prefeitura, os trabalhos estão concentrados em bairros como Coophatrabalho, Jardim Aero Rancho, Conjunto dos Rouxinóis, Centro e Cruzeiro.

Também há equipes no Jardim dos Estados, Carandá Bosque, Vila Rica, São Francisco, Jardim Botafogo e Mata do Jacinto.

Além dos trabalhos durante a semana, a operação inclui mutirões aos sábados. Em cada edição, são utilizadas, em média, 120 toneladas de massa asfáltica. Uma equipe permanece na região durante a semana seguinte para concluir os reparos.

O material utilizado é fornecido pelo Consórcio Central, tanto para as empresas contratadas quanto para as duas equipes próprias da Sisep.

Os contratos com as cinco empresas credenciadas somam R$ 46,3 milhões, com validade de um ano. Separadamente, a prefeitura informa que outros R$ 40 milhões são destinados aos serviços contínuos de tapa-buracos na cidade.

Os reparos também fazem parte do programa Vira CG Infraestrutura, que prevê mais de R$ 280 milhões em investimentos em 2026 para obras de pavimentação, drenagem, recapeamento, ciclovias e manutenção viária.

articles.title: Aguapés cobrem lagoa e indicam poluição por esgoto, diz biólogo | G1
articles.standfirst: Especialista alerta que a falta de oxigenação favorece a morte de organismos aquáticos e pode aumentar a proliferação de mosquitos transmissores de doenças.
articles.summary: A proliferação de aguapés na lagoa do Parque Matias Matos sinaliza despejo de esgoto, ameaça a vida aquática e aumenta o risco de doenças na região.
articles.body:
A Lagoa do Mocambinho, no Parque Ambiental Matias Matos, na Zona Norte de Teresina, está quase totalmente coberta por aguapés. Segundo especialistas, a proliferação das plantas está relacionada ao despejo de esgoto no local.

O g1 procurou a Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos (Semam) e a Superintendência de Desenvolvimento Urbano Norte (SDU Norte), mas não recebeu resposta até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A proliferação de aguapés indica a presença de grande quantidade de matéria orgânica na água. Além disso, a cobertura formada pelas plantas dificulta a oxigenação da lagoa e pode provocar a morte de peixes, o que causa mau cheiro na região.

Segundo o biólogo Wendell Kennedy, os aguapés funcionam como bioindicadores e sinalizam desequilíbrios ambientais no ecossistema.

O biólogo afirmou, em entrevista à TV Clube , que a recuperação da lagoa exige mais do que a retirada dos aguapés.

"Então a gente tem que atacar um problema por vez, medida paliativa inicial, fazendo remoção, expondo a lâmina d'água para a luminosidade, para acontecer a fotossíntese. E segundo ponto, atacar literalmente a causa principal do problema, que é o excesso de matéria orgânica dos esgotos que são lançados na região", explicou.

Aguapés cobrem lagoa da zona norte de Teresina — Foto: TV Clube

O especialista também alertou que o problema pode afetar a saúde de animais e pessoas.

"A gente pode ter superpopulações surgindo por causa desse desequilíbrio, assim como aumento da proliferação de mosquitos. Porque o peixe que vive nessa região vai se alimentar das larvas e ovos que são colocados [...] Se esses peixes estão morrendo sem a oxigenação que ficaria disponível para eles, justamente por causa dessa lâmina de aguapé que está impedindo, isso vai fazer com que a população de mosquitos exploda e essa superpopulação de mosquitos pode gerar a transmissão de doenças. Então, é um problema decorrendo de outro, justamente causando um efeito dominó", disse.

De acordo com Wendell Kennedy, o problema é recorrente não apenas no Parque Matias Matos, mas também em rios e outras regiões de Teresina.

*Juliana Cristina, estagiária sob supervisão de Carlienne Carpaso.

articles.title: Arábia Saudita ataca Sanaa; Houthis prometem resposta em Riade | G1
articles.standfirst: Ordens de evacuação para civis foram emitidas tanto pelas autoridades sauditas quanto pelos rebeldes do Iêmen para locais nas capitais dos dois países.
articles.summary: Ordens de evacuação para civis foram emitidas tanto pelas autoridades sauditas quanto pelos rebeldes do Iêmen para locais nas capitais dos dois países.
articles.body:
A Arábia Saudita atacou a Companhia de Petróleo do Iêmen , nos arredores da capital do país, Sanaa, nesta terça-feira (13).

O ataque foi noticiado pela Al-Masirah TV, controlada pelos Houthis, após a coalizão liderada pela Arábia Saudita ter emitido um alerta de evacuação das instalações, anunciando que faria uma operação militar no local.

Pouco antes do bombardeio, com o comunicado saudita, o grupo extremista do Iêmen advertiu que iria atacar novamente o aeroporto de Riade, assim como uma refinaria na capital e a sede da petroleira estatal Aramco em Dammam, se Saana fosse atingida.

Também pediu que civis deixassem esses 3 locais.

"As Forças Armadas iemenitas conclamam todos os cidadãos a abandonarem imediatamente e se afastarem dos alvos que nossas forças atacarão se o inimigo saudita chegar a atacar os locais anunciados na capital, Sanaa. As Forças Armadas do Iêmen alertam o inimigo saudita de que qualquer ataque será recebido com uma resposta dura e dolorosa na capital inimiga, Riade", escreveu o porta-voz militar do movimento na rede social X.

O gabinete da Arábia Saudita, presidido pelo príncipe herdeiro Mohammed bin Salman, afirmou que os houthis enfrentarão "consequências" por seus repetidos ataques ao reino, informou a mídia estatal saudita.

Desde sábado (11), os Houthis e a Arábia Saudita vêm trocando ataques e ameaças.

Um bombardeio contra o aeroporto de Riade, na capital saudita, que teve sua autoria reivindicada pelo grupo extremista ienamita deixou 12 mortos e cerca de 300 feridos .

Um dia após a tragédia, no domingo (11), os Houthis afirmaram que poderiam fazer novos ataques a aeroportos sauditas e divulgaram um comunicado orientando companhias aéreas, viajantes e funcionários para se manterem afastados desses locais.

Pouco depois, a coalizão liderada pela Arábia Saudita disse que um projétil não identificado havia atingido o terminal 4 do Aeroporto Internacional Rei Khalid.

"Reiteramos nosso alerta a todas as companhias aéreas, especialistas, funcionários, trabalhadores e viajantes contra o uso dos aeroportos e do espaço aéreo saudita, pois são vulneráveis ​​a ataques e se tornaram alvo de operações para nossas forças, com exceção dos aeroportos em Meca e Medina (cidades sagradas). Instamos a todos a levarem nossos avisos a sério, e a Arábia Saudita é responsável por quaisquer interceptações malsucedidas", diz o post.

No mesmo dia, segundo a Al Masirah TV, emissora controlada pelo grupo rebelde, um ataque foi realizado pela Arábia Saudita contra o Aeroporto Internacional de Sanaa, capital do Iêmen.

Nesta segunda, apesar de permanecer fechado, o aeroporto de Riade voltou a ser alvo dos Houthis, assim como a base aérea de Khamis Mushait , que teria sido atingida por um drone.

A Arábia Saudita afirmou, pouco antes, ter destruído um míssil balístico disparado pelo grupo em direção a Riade e um alerta de possível "ameaça hostil" foi enviado à população, segundo a agência de notícias Reuters.

Fumaça e chamas se elevam do Aeroporto Internacional Rei Khalid, após os houthis, apoiados pelo Irã, afirmarem ter atacado o aeroporto em Riad — Foto: Mídia Social/via REUTERS

articles.title: Oncoguia lança guia para orientar pacientes com câncer sobre uso seguro da inteligência artificial | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento, realizado entre julho e setembro de 2026, mostrou que 81% dos entrevistados gostariam de receber orientações sobre como utilizar a IA de maneira segura.
articles.summary: Levantamento, realizado entre julho e setembro de 2026, mostrou que 81% dos entrevistados gostariam de receber orientações sobre como utilizar a IA de maneira segura.
articles.body:
O Instituto Oncoguia lançou um guia para orientar pacientes com câncer sobre o uso seguro e responsável de ferramentas de inteligência artificial (IA). O material foi desenvolvido após uma pesquisa da organização identificar que 82% dos 1.186 participantes já utilizaram a tecnologia para buscar informações sobre saúde, câncer ou tratamento.

O levantamento, realizado entre julho e setembro de 2026, também mostrou que 81% dos entrevistados gostariam de receber orientações sobre como utilizar a IA de maneira segura.

Entre os 976 participantes que afirmaram utilizar inteligência artificial, 79,5% disseram recorrer à tecnologia para compreender resultados de exames, 67% para esclarecer dúvidas sobre o diagnóstico e 64% para buscar informações sobre efeitos colaterais e formas de aliviá-los.

Embora 93% tenham relatado que a IA ajudou a compreender melhor a doença ou o tratamento, 58% demonstraram preocupação com o risco de receber informações incorretas. O médico permanece como a principal referência para confirmar informações obtidas por meio dessas ferramentas, citado por 65% dos participantes.

articles.title: Plano de concessionária para Galeão prevê investimento de R$ 1 bi | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Aena, que ficará à frente do aeroporto até 2029, o projeto deve gerar 3.860 empregos no período e prevê ampliação de rotas. Ministro Tomé Franca disse que mais empresas aéreas devem operar para atrair novos públicos para o setor.
articles.summary: A Aena, nova concessionária responsável pelo Aeroporto do Galeão, anunciou nesta terça (13) um plano de investimentos de R$ 1 bilhão para os próximos 3 anos.
articles.body:
A Aena, nova concessionária responsável pelo Aeroporto Internacional Tom Jobim, o Galeão , anunciou nesta terça-feira (13) um plano de investimentos de R$ 1 bilhão para os próximos três anos. Segundo a empresa, o projeto deve gerar 3.860 empregos no período.

O anúncio foi feito durante a apresentação dos projetos de desenvolvimento do aeroporto. Durante o evento, o ministro de Portos e Aeroportos, Tomé Franca, afirmou que o Brasil precisa ampliar a oferta de rotas e o número de passageiros viajando para o país, com uma infraestrutura capaz de absorver o crescimento da demanda.

“O Brasil precisa de mais aeroportos vocacionados ao turismo internacional. Além do Aeroporto de Guarulhos, essa é a vocação do Aeroporto do Galeão. Pela infraestrutura e pela capacidade, mas também pela vocação da cidade e do estado do Rio de Janeiro , com suas belezas naturais e culturais, que são um motor do turismo do estado e do Brasil”, afirmou o ministro.

Tomé Franca, ministro de Portos e Aeroportos, durante evento no Aeroporto do Galeão na manhã desta terça-feira (13) — Foto: Alexandre Lima/ GloboNews

Franca também defendeu a abertura do mercado para novas companhias aéreas e a criação de um mercado aéreo comum entre os países da América do Sul.

“Queremos e merecemos mais, para que mais brasileiros possam viajar e para que haja maior diversidade de serviços. Isso ajudaria a atrair empresas low cost e ultra low cost, ampliando o acesso ao transporte aéreo”, disse.

O diretor-presidente da Aena Brasil, Santiago Yus, classificou o Galeão como uma infraestrutura estratégica para o turismo e o transporte de cargas no país. Segundo ele, o investimento de R$ 1 bilhão será realizado totalmente pela iniciativa privada.

Aeroporto Internacional Tom Jobim tem plano de investimento de R$ 1 bi em 3 anos — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

Segundo a Aena, os itens que passarão por manutenção ainda não foram definidos.

“É um aeroporto com grande potencial de crescimento. Não existe outra infraestrutura no Brasil que, em 2025, tenha movimentado 17 milhões de passageiros e disponha de capacidade para receber até 37 milhões por ano”, afirmou.

De acordo com cálculos da concessionária, cada R$ 1 investido no aeroporto gera um impacto de R$ 3,20 na economia do estado do Rio de Janeiro.

Desembarque internacional do Aeroporto Internacional Tom Jobim — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

O plano prevê o aumento da frequência de voos em 30 destinos, sendo 18 nacionais e 12 internacionais.

Ainda em outubro, estão previstos investimentos em rotas para Nova York e Toronto, além do aumento da frequência de voos para Paris e Miami.

Em novembro, deverão ser retomadas operações para Assunção, além do reforço na oferta de voos para Frankfurt, Lisboa e Porto.

Já em dezembro, o Galeão deverá receber mais voos vindos de cidades como Mendoza, Lima, Dallas e Montreal. O cronograma de expansão continuará ao longo do próximo ano.

A iniciativa também inclui a ampliação de rotas sazonais entre cidades brasileiras.

A Aena venceu, no fim de março, o leilão de venda assistida do Galeão com uma oferta de R$ 2,9 milhões. Com a incorporação do terminal, a empresa passa a administrar 18 aeroportos em dez estados brasileiros, com movimentação superior a 63 milhões de passageiros por ano.

articles.title: Obras do Complexo do Tarumã, em Curitiba, seguem atrasadas | G1
articles.standfirst: Até outubro de 2026, além da obra não estar finalizada, dados do portal da transparência mostram que projeto já ficou cerca de R$ 11 milhões mais caro.
articles.summary: Até outubro de 2026, além da obra não estar finalizada, portal da transparência mostra que projeto já ficou cerca de R$ 11 milhões mais caro.
articles.body:
A Prefeitura de Curitiba analisa um novo pedido de prorrogação do prazo para entrega das obras do Complexo do Tarumã, em Curitiba. A solicitação foi feita pela empreiteira contratada para o projeto, a Trail Infraestrutura, que não finalizou o serviço até agosto deste ano, data acordada na última negociação.

Inicialmente, as obras deveriam ser entregues entre março e abril de 2024 , mas já foram adiadas cinco vezes a pedido da empresa.

"Nós estamos analisando o pleito da empresa para a conclusão até janeiro. Um contrato nessa fase para nós não renovarmos implicaria fazer um novo processo licitatório, todo um diagnóstico novamente, então teríamos um uma condição de prazo muito maior", explicou o secretário de Obras Luiz Fernando Jamur em entrevista à RPC, afiliada da TV Globo .

O contrato para construção do Complexo do Tarumã foi assinado em outubro de 2022, no valor de R$ 92.382.636,50. A previsão para conclusão do projeto era em 540 dias, ou seja, entre março e abril de 2024.

Estação-tubo ainda não foi entregue no Complexo do Tarumã. — Foto: Foto: Reprodução/RPC

De acordo com a Secretaria Municipal de Obras Públicas, até o momento, foram homologados seis aditivos ao contrato, sendo cinco deles para prorrogação do prazo de execução da obra, com justificativa de questões técnicas, como necessidade de ajustes no projeto.

Segundo o órgão municipal, a maioria das justificativas apresentadas pela empreiteira não foram aceitas pela Administração Pública, gerando notificações e intimações. Já foram 250 notificações sobre assuntos diversos, como qualidade de execução dos serviços, cumprimento de cronograma, segurança e sinalização adequada.

Ainda, foram emitidas 34 intimações de penalidade por conta dos atrasos na execução da obra. Em alguns casos, inclusive, há decisão administrativa favorável à aplicação da penalidade de multa por atraso na execução do contrato, mas os valores não foram divulgados, pois os processos administrativos seguem em andamento.

Prefeitura informou que obras estão com 83% de conclusão. — Foto: Foto: Reprodução/RPC

Andamento das obras do Complexo do Tarumã

A Prefeitura de Curitiba informou que a execução das obras está em cerca de 83% . As faixas para circulação de veículos, com a duplicação do viaduto da Avenida Victor Ferreira do Amaral, foram implantadas e liberadas e, conforme o órgão, o viaduto já opera na capacidade máxima, incluindo as alças de acesso, sem bloqueios de trânsito.

"Todas as vias de circulação do viaduto estão concluídas e liberadas aos veículos, bem como todas as alças de acesso estão concluídas e liberadas aos veículos. Ou seja, o viaduto está funcionando na sua capacidade máxima viária estabelecida", disse Jamur.

canaleta exclusiva em concreto para uso do transporte coletivo (Linha Verde);

escadas e rampas de acesso para a integração da parte inferior (Avenida Victor Ferreira do Amaral) e superior do viaduto (Linha Verde);

confecção e instalação das estações-tubo (2 unidades sobre o viaduto);

acabamentos das praças Mauro Ferreira e Cova da Iria.

O g1 Paraná entrou em contato com a empreiteira responsável pelas obras, a Trail Infraestrutura, mas não houve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.summary: In early 2024, two of the biggest Silicon Valley companies -- Elon Musk's xAI and Meta -- fought to partner with a Generative AI company.
articles.body: In early 2024, two of the biggest Silicon Valley companies -- Elon Musk's xAI and Meta -- fought to partner with a Generative AI company. Meta and Elon Musk’s xAI competed for tie-up with chatbot-maker Character.ai, as deep-pocketed technology companies swarmed around the hottest artificial intelligence startups in Silicon Valley. Two years later, the same hotshot AI company, Character.ai, has filed for bankruptcy.Character.AI said on Monday it had filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the US. In a statement, dated October 12, the company said, "Today, we’re sharing that Character.ai has initiated a voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy process to facilitate a court-supervised sale of the company." The AI company said that it has begun the formal ​process to sell assets, including a license ​of certain intellectual property, through Chapter 11 and is ⁠seeking court approval for auction rules that would designate ​Disney as the lead, or stalking horse, bidder.Under this process, Disney's bid would set a baseline offer while allowing competing bidders to submit higher bids, and the company expects the sale process to conclude by late November or early December 2026. “After a comprehensive review of the available alternatives, the ‌board ⁠determined that this court-supervised sale process provides the company with the best opportunity to maximize value for all stakeholders," said Colin Adams, CEO of Character.AI.Character Technologies has listed estimated assets and liabilities between $50 million and $100 million, according ​to a court filing. The company said that it ​intends ⁠to continue operating its business, including the Character.AI platform, with minimal service disruptions during the sale process. If the ⁠process ​fails to produce a buyer ​willing to continue operating the platform, it will be shut down.When Meta and Elon Musk’s xAI 'fought' to partner with Character.aiAccording to a report in Financial Times, in May 2024, Meta and Elon Musk’s xAI sought partnership with chatbot-maker Character.ai. Facebook owner Meta reportedly held early discussions over a tie-up with Character.ai, which uses large language models to generate conversation in the style of various figures and personas, according to four people familiar with the matter. The groups discussed their top researchers working closely together on initiatives such as pre-training and developing models, said the report quoting sources.Character.ai also held exploratory talks with xAI over a similar partnership. Report claimed that the talks were focused on advancing research rather than an acquisition.Character.AI was founded by two former Google employees. In 2024, Google licensed the company’s technology and rehired the executives to work on generative AI products. A spokesman for Alphabet said that said the ⁠company played ​no role in developing Character.AI's products.Character.AI faced lawsuits over its chatbots encouraging users to do 'dangerous things'Earlier this year, a filing by Kentucky’s attorney general in a lawsuit claimed that Chatbots created by AI companion company Character.AI sometimes advised users to cut, starve or kill themselves. The lawsuit was filed in January with many specific allegations against the company blacked out. It alleged that the company’s products “were designed to entice children in ​a manner that prioritizes engagement over child wellbeing” and “encourages suicide, self-injury, isolation, and psychological manipulation.”The lawsuit calls Character.AI’s products defective. “Defendants have subjected Kentucky's children and residents to ​an ill-planned, uncontrolled ⁠experiment without any—let alone adequate or effective—safety measures,” it alleges.You use AI every day. articles.title: Why Muslim-majority Azerbaijan is restricting hijabs in schools
articles.summary: A country where around 96 percent of the population identifies as Muslim is witnessing protests after schools began turning away some girls and teachers
articles.body: A country where around 96 percent of the population identifies as Muslim is witnessing protests after schools began turning away some girls and teachers for wearing the hijab, triggering a debate over religious freedom and secular education in Azerbaijan.The restrictions have raised questions about why a Muslim-majority country is enforcing rules that prevent some hijab-wearing students from attending classes.According to an Al Jazeera, Azerbaijan's Cabinet of Ministers amended school uniform rules on September 21, prohibiting clothing that violates the prescribed dress code or conflicts with the secular principle of general education.Although the regulation does not explicitly name the hijab, its enforcement has reportedly led to some hijab-wearing students and teachers being turned away from schools, prompting protests and class boycotts.Teacher Zahra Hasanova, who was reportedly told she could no longer wear the hijab at school, described the decision as deeply upsetting, while defending the right to choose whether to wear the headscarf.“To be honest, I am a little emotional. I am hurt,” Hasanova told Al Jazeera. “[The hijab] is a personal choice, and if one day I want to take it off, that should be my choice too.”Local media outlets reported that students at least two schools boycotted classes in protest against the restrictions. Videos circulated online showed students crying and embracing teachers as they were turned away from schools.Why Azerbaijan is enforcing the hijab restrictionsAzerbaijan's government has justified the new restrictions on the grounds of secular education, a uniform school dress code and professional standards for teachers.According to the state-run Azerbaijani Press Agency (APA), the September 21 amendment to school uniform rules was intended to establish a common dress code consistent with the secular principle of general education.A separate decision on October 6 introduced clothing requirements for teachers, emphasising neatness, professionalism and suitability for the school environment.The legal basis for the government's position lies in Article 18 of Azerbaijan's Constitution, which separates religion from the state and requires the state education system to be secular. However, Article 48 also protects freedom of conscience and the right to practise a religion, while Article 42 guarantees the right to education.Although around 96 percent of Azerbaijan's population identifies as Muslim, the country is constitutionally secular. The government has presented the rules as an education policy rather than an explicitly anti-Islamic measure.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: CJP: India 'cockroach' leaders detained after entering barricaded protest site
articles.summary: Protesters climbed over barricades in central Delhi to demand the election chief resign over revised voter lists.
articles.body:
Leaders of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) were detained early on Tuesday after they entered a heavily-guarded protest site and chanted slogans demanding the country's election chief resign over a controversial revision of electoral rolls.

Party founder Abhijeet Dipke shared a video showing Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das being taken away by police from Jantar Mantar, a historic Delhi observatory popular for protests.

Footage showed the two - along with others - climbing over police barricades before chanting slogans while holding the Indian flag.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi's opponents allege the voter list revision benefits his party, a charge it and the Election Commission reject.

There have been days of protests demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.

Police have stepped up security across Delhi as demonstrators challenge restrictions on where protests can be held.

Early on Tuesday, Dipke, Das and Ranka all shared videos showing Das and Ranka entering Jantar Mantar.

"You cannot denotify the resistance," Dipke wrote on X.

Das also posted a message declaring that the site had been "reclaimed" and that they were being detained.

It was not immediately clear where police had taken the leaders.

Ranka later appeared on an Instagram live broadcast from a police bus alongside other detainees where they appeared cheerful and said they would not back down.

The detentions came a day after the federal home ministry announced that Jantar Mantar, long associated with public protests in Delhi, would no longer be a designated protest venue. Authorities instead identified three alternative locations where demonstrations can be held with permission.

Before the decision, the CJP had met Delhi Police officials to seek permission for a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar and had warned that it would announce further demonstrations if it received no response.

"30 mins after we went to Delhi Police asking for a date when we can go to Jantar Mantar, Jantar Mantar was de-notified as a protest site," Ranka had earlier posted on X.

Most of the party's leadership has been in Delhi in recent days. Dipke, however, had travelled to his hometown in Maharashtra after the death of his grandmother. He was among several CJP leaders detained ahead of a planned demonstration on Saturday and was released the next day.

The CJP had called for a protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, but authorities imposed extensive security restrictions across the capital to prevent demonstrators from reaching the site.

Several metro stations were closed, train services were disrupted and thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were deployed.

Over the weekend, the police detained and released thousands of people, including several journalists. Some videos and photos from the protest show police dragging people, including women, by force and pushing them into buses.

Separately, opposition parties held a march in Delhi on Monday from Connaught Place - a major shopping district in the heart of the capital - to the Supreme Court.

The Congress, India's main opposition party, also petitioned the Supreme Court on Monday, challenging the Election Commission's voter revision exercise, which has resulted in tens of millions of names being removed from electoral rolls.

Critics say the exercise risks excluding eligible voters and making it harder for them to prove their eligibility.

Anger over the revision exercise intensified after The Indian Express reported that Kumar had disregarded concerns raised by the two other election commissioners over changes to voter registration. The Election Commission has said its decisions were unanimous.

The current protests follow student-led demonstrations earlier this year over exam irregularities and demands for education reforms.

The CJP led weeks of action that culminated in the resignation of federal Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

The group began as online satire after India's Chief Justice Surya Kant compared some unemployed young people to cockroaches during a court hearing in May. He later said his remarks had been misinterpreted, but the comments had already become a rallying cry for young people seeking change.

After the summer protests, the CJP evolved into a pressure group, tapping into wider anger over unemployment, exam irregularities and government accountability.

articles.title: Taylor Swift donates $1 million to heart charity in honour of her father Scott Swift; US projections warn 6 in 10 adults could have cardiovascular disease by 2050s
articles.summary: Taylor Swift’s latest charitable contribution is tied to a health issue that has affected her own family.
articles.body: Taylor Swift’s latest charitable contribution is tied to a health issue that has affected her own family. The singer has donated $1 million to the American Heart Association in 2025 , directing attention towards cardiovascular disease, its treatment and the work needed to prevent it. The gift honours her father, Scott Swift, whose heart condition she discussed earlier this year. The money is intended to support scientific research, prevention programmes and access to care, according to the organisation. Her contribution also comes as health officials warn that cardiovascular disease is likely to affect a growing share of the American population over the coming decades, placing greater demands on healthcare services.Taylor Swift’s $1 million gift draws on her family’s experience with heart diseaseSwift’s contribution recognises her father’s experience with heart disease and supports the American Heart Association’s work across research, public education and medical care. The organisation has not presented the gift as funding for a single project. Instead, it is intended to advance its wider efforts to reduce the burden of cardiovascular disease, including work on prevention and improving access to life-saving treatment.As reported by American Heart Association, Nancy Brown, the association’s chief executive, said, “Taylor Swift’s remarkable generosity will create lasting change far beyond its financial value.”She also pointed, “Her family’s experience with cardiovascular disease is all too common, affecting nearly half of American adults. Her commitment to supporting her father will make so many others aware of the need to take their own heart health seriously, strengthen prevention efforts, and improve controllable risk factors—ultimately helping more people live longer, healthier lives.”Swift has previously discussed her family’s experience with cardiovascular disease on the New Heights podcast. Her father’s condition has given the donation a personal connection, although the charity’s work extends well beyond individual cases.What the money will supportThe American Heart Association funds scientific research and works to improve how cardiovascular conditions are prevented, identified and treated. Swift’s $1 million gift is intended to advance these efforts, alongside initiatives designed to help more people receive appropriate care.Better understanding of cardiovascular disease can inform clinical practice and contribute to improved treatments. Prevention is another focus, particularly because many of the risk factors associated with heart disease can be identified before a serious event occurs. The association also works to make medical guidance and health information more widely available, with programmes intended to reach communities where access to care may be limited.The organisation's activities include training people in cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), publishing medical guidelines, supporting health policy and educating the public about cardiovascular risks. Its work covers more than the treatment of people who have already developed heart disease. It also aims to reduce the likelihood that people will develop serious conditions in the first place.Why prevention remains a major part of the association’s workHeart disease and stroke together account for a substantial share of deaths in the United States. The American Heart Association identifies cardiovascular disease as a leading public health challenge, with risk factors ranging from high blood pressure and elevated cholesterol to smoking, physical inactivity and poor nutrition.Some risks are linked to family history, which can make it important for people to understand their relatives’ medical backgrounds. Others can be monitored through routine checks and addressed with medical advice or changes to daily habits. Blood pressure, cholesterol and blood glucose levels are among the measures healthcare professionals use to assess cardiovascular risk.The association advises people to discuss their family history and individual risk factors with a doctor rather than waiting for symptoms to appear. Regular physical activity, a balanced diet, avoiding tobacco and managing stress can also form part of a preventive approach.According to the association, nearly 80% of heart disease cases may be preventable through healthy behaviours. That estimate underlines the emphasis it places on early intervention, although prevention does not remove every risk or guarantee that someone will avoid cardiovascular disease.Swift’s donation supports an organisation that combines research and treatment initiatives with this kind of public guidance. Its aim is to reduce the number of people who develop serious cardiovascular conditions and improve outcomes for those who do.How they support patients and families beyond treatmentThe association has also used the wider conversation around Swift’s donation to encourage people to take cardiovascular health seriously within their own families. Brown referred to the singer’s familiar heart-hand gesture, connecting it with the organisation’s efforts to recognise those affected by heart disease, including relatives and partners who support them.For the charity, the message is closely linked to its public health work: personal experiences can prompt conversations about family history, screening and the steps people can take to understand their own risk.The American Heart Association expects cardiovascular disease to become an even greater burden as the country's population changes and risk factors remain widespread. Its projections indicate that at least six in 10 Americans could have some form of cardiovascular disease within 30 years.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge
articles.summary: A group of clinicians warns technology use in English schools is driving a rise in health problems like short-sightedness.
articles.body:
The amount of time children in England spend on screens at school could be harming their "physical and developmental health", a group of more than 150 clinicians has warned.

GPs, paediatricians and other specialists said in an open letter to Education Secretary Lucy Powell and Health Secretary Yvette Cooper that tablets and laptops are being used without a full understanding of their long-term health impacts, including on eye health.

The clinicians said they are prescribing glasses, hearing aids and speech therapy to children "for a problem that is unintentionally being made worse in our schools".

The government said it was consulting on screen time guidance for children aged five to 18 but that technology could be a powerful learning tool if used properly.

The group of clinicians said nearly one million children are using screens in most lessons, despite studies suggesting a rise in short-sightedness.

They pointed to an analysis of 276 studies covering 5.4 million participants around the world.

That analysis, they claimed, found a rise in short-sightedness among children and adolescents from around 24% in 1990 to almost 36% by 2023, warning the condition is associated with an increased risk of a range of eye health problems.

Many children now spend longer on screens in the classroom than is recommended in a 24-hour period, the letter said, adding: "As a country, we need to wake up to this now, and start rolling back screen use in schools before the damage compounds further."

One of its signatories was Dr Becky Foljambe, an NHS GP and founder of Health Professionals for Safer Screens. She told BBC Radio 4's Today programme parents had not been given the chance to "opt out" of the "excessive" use of screens in schools, which risks children "just not thriving" in education.

She said an "explosion" in short-sightedness "cannot be put down to genetics alone".

Foljambe said it was a "lazy argument" to advocate for screen use to prepare children for a digital world, adding: "They also need their sleep, their eyesight, they need rest, they need ability to critically think and appraise."

WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

More children and teenagers enjoying reading for first time in 5 years

"We are conscious that some of this evidence is still surfacing but the direction of travel is consistent across multiple, independent, and in some cases very large, bodies of research," the letter continued.

It also warned that children with special educational needs are "disproportionately" directed to screen-based learning.

Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said education technology can provide schools with "very effective learning tools".

But he said such technology was only part of an "overall learning strategy", which also includes classroom discussion and interaction, and that the school day also has "plenty of non-screen time such as PE, sport, and break times with classmates".

"We would welcome the development of practical, evidence-based guidance to support the work of schools in the use of education technology," he added.

Paul Whiteman, general secretary of the National Association of Head Teachers, said it was "important that a healthy balance is struck", adding that "greater clarity is needed from the government on this".

A Department for Education spokesperson said the government was developing new screen-time guidance for children aged five to 18, and will consult on the safety of artificial intelligence and educational technology in schools.

They said: "Used well, technology can be a powerful tool to support learners who need it and free up teachers to deliver the excellent education every child deserves."

It comes after a ban on smartphones in schools in England came into force in June, making individual schools and trusts legally responsible for being phone-free throughout the day.

articles.title: Trust running Shambellie House near Dumfries to cease trading
articles.summary: It says running Shambellie House near Dumfries has become "simply unsustainable" due to rising costs.
articles.body:
The trust which took over Scotland's former national museum of costume has announced it will cease trading in January.

Shambellie House at New Abbey near Dumfries closed in 2013, with its contents transferred to Edinburgh.

A trust was set up two years later to find a new use for the building and it was handed over in 2021.

Shambellie House Trust (SHT) vice-chair, Ann Hill, said it was solvent, but insurance, heating and electricity were too expensive. If a new charity cannot be found to take over the site, it will be sold and the proceeds returned to the Scottish government.

Trust takes control of former costume museum

How fashion returned to Scotland's former national costume museum

When plans were announced to shut the costume museum more than a decade ago it provoked cross-party political opposition.

National Museums Scotland said that it had taken the decision "with great regret" to shut the facility, which first opened to the public in 1982.

The trust was set up to try to bring it back into use and eventually reopened it as an arts and heritage centre in 2022.

However, the building now faces an uncertain future once again.

Hill said the trust had come to the decision "with great sadness" to cease trading on 10 January next year.

She said they had enjoyed the company of many tutors, speakers, events and pupils over the years and thanked them for their support.

However, she said running costs had risen "spectacularly" which had put "enormous strains" on everyone trying to keep the project working but it had become "simply unsustainable".

The SHT will now look for another charity to take over the building. Any bid would need to be approved by the Scottish government which transferred the property to the trust.

If it is unable to find a new operator, then the house and land would be sold.

Hill told BBC Scotland News the building had been in a "sad, sorry state" when the trust took over and it had been struggling almost since the outset to find enough money to look after it.

She said that in recent times things had become even more problematic and the issue was widespread.

"This past year we have seen a lack of money being the most difficult thing for people," she said.

"Even with the quilt show this past week, we've had people that didn't come and phone up to say they were sorry they couldn't come from the likes of Fife or Stirling because petrol was too expensive.

"So it is not just us, it is the whole country that is feeling it and I see more charities winding up than ever before."

She stressed that they were still solvent and did not owe "anybody anything".

articles.title: Mapping Africa’s energy wealth and 560 million who remain without power
articles.summary: Africa is rich in energy, yet hundreds of millions Africans still live without electricity, most of the world’s total.
articles.body:
Africa holds billions of barrels of oil, trillions of cubic metres of gas and produces most of the world’s cobalt and manganese for electric car batteries.

This week, energy ministers, investors and oil executives are meeting in Cape Town for African Energy Week, which runs until October 16. The conference focuses on investment in oil and gas, energy finance and ending energy poverty.

In this visual explainer, Al Jazeera maps where Africa’s oil, gas and critical minerals are found, how its electricity is generated and who still goes without it.

Africa holds about 125 billion barrels of proven crude oil reserves, representing 7.2 percent of the global total. Proven reserves are oil that has been discovered and can be extracted commercially with existing technology, but is still in the ground.

Libya and Nigeria account for nearly 70 percent of Africa’s reserves, with 48.4 billion and 36.9 billion barrels, respectively. Algeria ranks third, with 12.2 billion barrels. Angola follows with 7.78 billion barrels, while South Sudan and Egypt hold 3.75 billion and 3.3 billion barrels, respectively.

Nigeria was Africa’s largest oil producer in 2024, accounting for about 23 percent of the continent’s output. Algeria and Angola followed with about 17 percent each, and together the three produced 56 percent of Africa’s oil. The top five producers accounted for more than 80 percent. Africa as a whole produced 7.6 percent of the world’s crude oil, roughly in line with its share of global reserves.

Libya, which holds Africa’s largest proven reserves, ranked only fourth in production. Italy’s Eni, France’s TotalEnergies and Spain’s Repsol are among the foreign companies operating in the country, where political disputes and blockades have repeatedly disrupted output.

Where are Africa’s natural gas reserves?

Africa held almost 18 trillion cubic metres of proven natural gas reserves at the end of 2023.

Nigeria and Algeria hold about 58 percent of the total, followed by Mozambique with 2.84 trillion cubic metres, Egypt with 2.21 trillion and Libya with 1.51 trillion.

Algeria and Nigeria are also among Africa’s leading gas exporters, while much of Mozambique’s reserves, discovered offshore in the 2010s, remain largely undeveloped.

Where do the critical minerals come from?

The African continent supplies a large share of the minerals used in electric vehicles, batteries and renewable energy technologies.

In 2025, African countries accounted for 71.2 percent of global cobalt production and 72.4 percent of manganese production.

Cobalt is used in rechargeable batteries. Manganese is mainly used to strengthen steel, but it is also used in some electric vehicle batteries and in batteries that store renewable energy.

The Democratic Republic of the Congo produces nearly 70 percent of the world’s cobalt. Some of it is dug by hand by artisanal miners, and Amnesty International has documented dangerous and often deadly conditions in some of the country’s mines.

South Africa produces nearly 38 percent of global manganese, followed by Gabon with nearly 25 percent. Together with Ghana, the three countries account for 72.4 percent of global production.

Zimbabwe, Africa’s largest lithium producer, accounted for 9.6 percent of global production in 2025. Lithium is used in rechargeable batteries that power electric vehicles and store electricity from solar and wind.

Madagascar, Mozambique and Tanzania produced a combined 222,000 tonnes of natural graphite in 2025, or 11.9 percent of the global total. Graphite is used in the anodes of most lithium-ion batteries, the negative electrodes that store and release energy, as well as in steel manufacturing, lubricants and pencils.

How many African countries produce electricity from renewables?

Renewable energy accounted for all electricity generated in Ethiopia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024. Uganda, Namibia and Eswatini each generated more than 96 percent from renewables, mostly hydropower.

At the other end, renewables made up less than 5 percent in Algeria, Libya, Niger and Tunisia, which rely mainly on gas or oil.

Ethiopia’s electricity comes mostly from hydropower, led by the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Blue Nile, Africa’s largest hydroelectric project. The dam began generating power in 2022 and was officially inaugurated in September 2025.

Where do people have access to electricity?

In 2024, six African countries reported universal electricity access: Algeria, Egypt, Mauritius, Morocco, Seychelles and Tunisia. Together, they are home to about 215 million people, or roughly 14 percent of Africa’s population.

Elsewhere, access varies widely. In South Sudan, only 5.4 percent of people had electricity. The figure was 15.6 percent in Malawi and 22.5 percent in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, even though the DRC generates all its power from renewables.

Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, had an access rate of 62.5 percent, leaving roughly 85 million people without electricity, the largest number of any country in the world.

In rural areas, where access is far lower than in cities, many families still rely on kerosene lamps, candles or torches to light their homes after dark.

Africa has vast energy resources, from oil and natural gas to the minerals powering the global energy transition. Yet more than 560 million people in sub-Saharan Africa lack access to electricity, accounting for about 86 percent of the global total, according to the World Health Organization (WHO) .

articles.title: Bulgarian PM summons Russian ambassador after ship sinks in Black Sea drone attack
articles.summary: Six crew members are rescued but 10 are missing after a merchant ship was sunk overnight, Bulgaria says.
articles.body:
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev has summoned the Russian ambassador after two merchant ships were struck by drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast and one of them sank.

Six crew members on the Guinea-Bissau-flagged HS Dignity were rescued and 10 others are missing, according to Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov, after it went down 17 nautical miles (31km) east of the village of Krapets having sent a distress signal.

The other ship, the Ukrainian owned Chelsea-3, was hit by drones 18 nautical miles from the town of Byala and all 15 crew were rescued.

The attacks come a week after two other commercial ships were hit by sea and aerial drones in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone.

One of the ships, the Alfa Watan, sank and all 10 crew, including nine Syrians, are presumed dead.

Radev convened an emergency meeting on Tuesday and said he had summoned Russian envoy Eleonora Mitrofanova. Although there was no conclusive evidence of blame on "either side... the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation", he said.

Mitrofanova was later quoted by Bulgarian media as telling Radev she had no information from Russia's defence ministry relating to the latest attacks. She also said these strikes could have been a provocation by a third party.

Bulgaria is a Nato member, and Radev also spoke to secretary general Mark Rutte about the latest attacks.

"Nato will continue to work closely with our allies in the Black Sea," Rutte said after the talks.

"We have already strengthened our posture along the eastern flank and will continue to monitor the security environment, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed," he added.

The Dignity and Chelsea-3 were struck just outside Bulgarian territorial waters, in its Black Sea "exclusive economic zone".

If this had happened just a few nautical miles to the west, Article 5 of the Nato treaty could have been triggered. The article defines an armed attack on one member of the military alliance as an attack on all.

"Escalation in the Black Sea is steadily increasing," Bulgaria's defence minister later told reporters after speaking to his counterparts in Romania and Turkey. "We see this conflict drawing ever closer to our territorial waters."

"We assume the drones are Russian," he said, as it would have been "illogical" for Ukraine to target its own ships.

Rumen Radev had earlier asked Nato and the EU for technical assistance in investigating the previous attacks that took place on 6 October, indicating it was unclear who was behind them.

Radev came to office during the summer and although he has rejected suggestions that he is "pro-Russian", his government has until now avoided blaming Moscow.

Ukraine has directly accused Russia of staging the latest attacks and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen spoke on Tuesday of the Black Sea becoming "another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine. This is unacceptable".

Russia's military has not publicly commented on the issue. It has recently intensified its strikes on vessels in the Black Sea, particularly the western side, as part of its war against Ukraine.

The same day that two ships were targeted off Bulgaria last week, Ukraine hit an oil tanker in the Russian Black Sea port of Sochi.

Moscow says it is targeting ships delivering weapons and dual-use cargo to Ukrainian ports - and cited attacks in the ports of Mykolaiv and Chornomorsk last week, along with one in the Black Sea.

However, Kyiv and its European allies say merchant vessels carrying grain and other civilian cargo are being attacked.

Meeting his security chiefs on Tuesday, Bulgaria's prime minister said: "Another attack on merchant ships in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters is absolutely unacceptable".

While the search continued for the rest of the crew from the HS Dignity, Radev said five crew members on board the Chelsea-3 were being treated for minor injuries. The cargo ship is registered in the southern Ukraine port of Odesa.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said "Russia's latest attack on commercial vessels near Bulgaria's territorial waters... once again demonstrates Moscow's deliberate disregard for civilian lives and maritime security in the Black Sea".

"The Black Sea is a lifeline for global food security. Russia is attacking it to weaponise hunger and hold the world hostage. This must be met with strength," he added.

Both Russia and Ukraine are major grain-exporting countries and Turkey has called on both countries to halt attacks in the Black Sea.

Moscow has repeatedly rejected calls by the US and Europe for a naval ceasefire in the Black Sea, blaming Ukraine for attacking Russian merchant ships in the area.

Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory.

articles.title: ELI STEELE: NYC ICE shooting exposes how White guilt erases personal responsibility
articles.summary: The Oscar Belgal ICE shooting in Marble Hill, New York, has sparked a national debate over White guilt, individual responsibility, and immigrant accountability.
articles.body: Editor's note: Eli Steele's latest film "White Guilt" was released on Oct. 6. Find out more here. School had just let out in Marble Hill, a small enclave of Manhattan bordering the Bronx. It was a little after 4 p.m. on Oct. 8 when Oscar Belgal, 28, picked up his 5-year-old son and began backing his Honda CR-V into a parking spot on a crowded street. A police camera caught what happened next. Two men dressed in plain clothes approached Belgal’s SUV with their guns drawn — one to the driver’s side, the other to the front. They were ICE officers. More agents were part of the operation, and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani later noted that officers surrounding the vehicle wore construction vests and masks. Belgal responded by pulling the SUV forward out of the space. As he did, one officer punched and broke the driver’s window, but Belgal managed to drive off and out of the camera’s view. FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS DEPORTATION OF DOMINICAN ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SHOT BY ICE DURING NYC ARREST ATTEMPT The ICE officers caught up with Belgal about a block away. According to ICE officials, Belgal refused orders to exit the vehicle, turned his SUV into a weapon and rammed two government cars. Belgal's defense attorney disputes this account, maintaining that Belgal fled out of panic to protect his child from unidentified, armed men. Initial NYPD street camera footage did not capture the moment of the shooting, but investigators later determined that a bullet went through Belgal's windshield. At least one officer fired seven rounds, striking Belgal in the neck below his left ear. His son, sitting in the back seat, was not physically hurt. The FBI, Homeland Security investigators and the Bronx District Attorney’s office have all launched inquiries into the shooting. MAMDANI CALLS ICE A 'ROGUE' AGENCY AFTER NYC SHOOTING, CLAIMS AGENTS VIEW LAW AS 'MERELY A SUGGESTION' But there is a second story here, one that reveals where we are as a nation. Within hours of the shooting, Oscar Belgal was no longer a man, an individual. He became a symbol. And the people who made him into a symbol did so by taking away the very thing that makes a man a man: responsibility for what he does. First, Belgal was not a stranger to the justice system. In 2023, according to a criminal complaint, he was driving with two passengers in his back seat when he turned, pointed a gun at them and demanded their jewelry. They complied. Belgal pleaded guilty and received five years of probation. In December 2025, he was indicted on 10 counts related to narcotics distribution; he pleaded not guilty and was released on supervised conditions. Federal officials state that he is in the country illegally and allege that he has ties to the Trinitarios gang. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has stated that when ICE previously attempted to arrest him in September, Belgal fled. When New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch laid out that record, the reaction from the left was not to weigh it. Instead, its leading figures declared all of Belgal’s criminal history irrelevant. ELI STEELE: THE TERROR OF BEING CALLED RACIST IS CRUSHING FREE SPEECH IN AMERICA Darializa Avila Chevalier, a Democratic Socialists of America candidate for Congress in New York's 13th District, went on Hasan Piker's stream to talk about the shooting. When Piker asked about Belgal's criminal history, she said, "To me, it doesn't even matter." She then turned her wrath on Tisch and accused her of trying to "villainize Oscar." She demanded her resignation. Then she asked the audience to "put yourself in Oscar's shoes." Masked men were coming at his car and "You're running," she said. "I'm sorry, you're protecting your child." She ended with, "F--- ICE and abolish it." What struck me was her moral outrage. She was outraged that stating a man’s record in a matter-of-fact way was now the equivalent of "villainizing" him. All that mattered to Chevalier was that he was an immigrant, a Dominican like her, a member of an oppressed group, and that he was being chased by men with guns who were ICE. In my new film, "White Guilt," my father, Shelby Steele, the author, columnist and Hoover Institution Fellow, shows how the left created a world where responsibility can never be demanded of the oppressed. He describes going to a Black Power rally on the South Side of Chicago to hear the comedian and activist Dick Gregory: "Gregory argued that a racist America had given us responsibility, but had denied us the freedom to do much with it," my father says in the film. "Gregory held a Marxian vision of racism as a systemic force that made responsibility irrelevant in the struggle against oppression. Thus, it was bad manners to ask a black to lift themselves up." MAMDANI DEMANDS TRUMP RELEASE ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SHOT BY ICE AGENT AS PROTESTS ERUPT IN THE BRONX Then Lyndon Johnson stood up at Howard University and said you do not take a man hobbled by chains, bring him to the starting line and tell him he is free to compete. "By implication, Johnson agreed with Gregory," my father says. "Suddenly, if you were black living in this new age of white guilt, you could not be expected to carry the same responsibilities as others." The belief Gregory preached and Johnson blessed, that oppression made responsibility irrelevant, became one of the core tenets of the white guilt racial order we live under today. White guilt is not the guilt a person feels for something he did. It is not personal, which is why I tire of hearing people declare, "I have no White guilt." White guilt is the collective guilt that the left assigns to all Whites for America's past racial sins. What it produces is not remorse but terror, the terror of being called a racist and losing your moral authority. To escape that terror, the "oppressor" buys back his innocence by asking nothing of the "oppressed," and the "oppressed" are handed power so long as they remain victims. That is how responsibility became "bad manners," in the words of my father, and demanding accountability became racism. HOCHUL BOASTS 'I JUST BANNED IT' AS NEW YORK OUTLAWS LOCAL POLICE PARTNERSHIPS WITH ICE Today the "oppressor system" is America itself, and ICE is its face. And what the formula needs most is a symbol. Activists like Avila Chevalier dehumanize the oppressed by stripping away their responsibility and accountability, then wield what is left as a cudgel against the oppressor system. Once Belgal's record was erased, all that remained was an immigrant father shot by ICE with his little boy in the car. Between them, Avila Chevalier and Mayor Zohran Mamdani demanded that ICE be abolished, the police commissioner resign, Belgal be released and immigration enforcement halt across the city. They did not demand anything of Oscar Belgal. The DSA often calls itself the party of the people, but listen to how it talks about the people it claims to defend. Its words for them are almost always the oppressed, the victims and the impoverished. Their value to the movement is not their individual humanity but what they collectively symbolize. If the DSA draws its power from these symbols of oppression to milk White guilt, why would it ever surrender this power? There is one innocent in all of this: the 5-year-old boy in the back seat. His mother says he has nightmares and won’t speak despite his talkative nature. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION The young boy will grow up with two stories of that fateful afternoon. In one version, his father will be seen as a victim, nothing more, and the world owes him. In the other story, his father is an individual who made choices, some of them bad, and yet has the chance to improve his life somehow. It is the second story that gives the young boy a real chance at life. Belgal’s lawyer said the first thing that his client asked was whether his son was OK. This detail reveals to us that Oscar Belgal is a man with a conscience, and a man with a conscience can bear responsibility for his choices. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The same lawyer said that "regardless of whether or not someone has a criminal history, it is not lawful, and it's not okay to shoot a father." The investigations will decide whether the shooting was lawful, and due process, which protects all individuals within this country, including those who are not citizens. So let the courts judge the officer who fired, and let them judge Oscar Belgal too. Avila Chevalier would cry that this is villainizing him. Those who believe in American principles would call it treating him like a man who is responsible for his own life. The activists will never allow it. Their power in White guilt America depends on keeping Oscar Belgal a permanent symbol of oppression. But what good has ever come out of dehumanization? CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM ELI STEELE

articles.title: Welsh government and Labour in mini-budget deal with £60m for ALN
articles.summary: The Plaid Cymru-led administration had failed to pass its spending plans during the summer.
articles.body:
The Welsh government has reached a deal with Labour on its mini-budget, which had failed to pass in the summer.

Ministers said the Plaid Cymru-led administration had now agreed an extra £60m for the education of children with additional learning needs (ALN).

Labour, which sits in opposition after losing May's Senedd election, had rejected a £40m a year deal across three years, in angry scenes at the Welsh Parliament in the last week of term in July.

Welsh Labour leader Ken Skates had demanded £100m this year when the supplementary budget was last discussed.

Reform said the deal was good for Plaid and Labour but not Wales.

Despite the agreement with Labour, headteachers union NAHT expressed "deep disappointment" at the level of funding.

Drakeford says Labour made mistakes in failed mini-budget talks

The budget will be debated in the Senedd on 3 November.

On Tuesday, First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth said: "This agreement reflects what can be achieved when parties across the Senedd work together."

Skates said Labour had "managed to secure a significant cash injection for schools".

"While we still believe the Welsh government should be setting aside more for ALN in schools, it is a welcome first step in dealing with the need to better fund schools," he said.

Plaid Cymru's original mini-budget included £100m for the NHS to bring down waiting times, £55m for childcare and £40m for school repairs.

If the supplementary budget is not passed then the government would have to find other ways to fund its new plans.

Helen Jenner, leader of Reform Wales, said: "While we welcome extra support for additional learning needs provision, the Welsh government is still sending millions of pounds of taxpayers' money overseas while our public services suffer here at home."

Former Welsh Labour leader Mark Drakeford previously said his party had made mistakes in how it handled negotiations with Plaid over the summer, and suggested there was a case to be made to take the money that had been previously offered by Plaid.

Following Tuesday's announcement, Llŷr Powell, Reform's chief whip, said: "When Mark Drakeford speaks, Ken Skates starts dancing."

Darren Millar, leader of the Welsh Conservatives in the Senedd, said the deal was "merely a continuation of the same failed budget approach by the Labour-Plaid duopoly that has been letting down the people of Wales for decades".

It is not known yet if Labour will vote for or abstain on the budget as part of the deal.

If Labour abstain Plaid would need the support of the Greens and Lib Dem MS Jane Dodds

Skates did not say which way his party would go, telling BBC Wales on Tuesday: "We're going to make a final decision on that but certainly we will not stop the budget from passing."

ALN is the equivalent education system in Wales to special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) in England.

The Welsh government received extra cash as a result of more SEND spending in England to help schools struggling with debt, and Labour had argued for some of that to be given to schools in Wales.

Rob Kelsall, assistant general secretary of NAHT, said school leaders across Wales would be asking "what happened to the £322m that became available to Wales as a result of additional SEND funding in England?"

He said: "What has emerged is a package that falls substantially short of that figure and asks schools to be grateful for receiving only a fraction of what should have been available to learners with additional needs."

Welsh Education Minister, Anna Brychan, said ministers remained in "active discussions" with NAHT Cymru.

She said ALN was a "key priority" for her, and she recognised the "significant financial and operational pressures" facing schools and colleges.

"It is my hope that this additional funding, to be used in-year, will alleviate some of the more immediate financial and operational pressures facing schools, colleges, local authorities and support services," she added.

There were angry scenes in the Senedd in July when the Plaid Cymru government brought its supplementary budget to a vote without a deal in place.

Plaid failed to get any opposition support for the package.

Finance Minister Elin Jones accused Labour of behaving as a "destructive opposition" at the time.

Tory Senedd leader Millar said the decision to vote on the budget anyway was "bonkers".

The first minister later said his government had learned "lessons" from the episode, and promised to improve the way his government engaged with others.

It was not clear if the £60m offered in the deal is annual, and Brychan said allocation for future years would be part of the preparations for the draft budget for 2027-28.

Talks are ongoing with other parties for the Welsh government's full annual spending plans, which will be voted on by the Senedd early next year.

Of the £60m, £56m will be split between schools and councils - 80% to schools and 20% to councils.

Another £1.5m will be spent on a long-term sustainability plan, and £2.5m for the further education sector.

articles.title: One killed, several injured in Georgia rollercoaster ‘incident’
articles.summary: Six Flags temporarily closes nine similar rollercoasters after a fatal accident at its Georgia amusement park.
articles.body:
A person has died and several others have been injured in an incident involving a rollercoaster at an amusement park in the state of Georgia in the United States.

The incident happened on Monday at the Six Flags amusement park, about 15 miles (24km) northwest of Atlanta.

Officials are investigating the death but have yet to confirm its nature or how the others were injured.

Images and videos have been circulating online that appear to show a man who seems to have been ejected from his seat and landed on the ground.

Al Jazeera has not independently verified the footage.

Six Flags has since closed nine rollercoasters at six of its parks “out of an abundance of caution”, a spokesperson said, adding that they are similar to the one involved in the incident.

Police and the company did not name the ride, but local TV footage showed passengers being escorted off the Goliath rollercoaster, which stopped halfway through the ride.

Witnesses also told local station 11Alive that they saw a man land on the roof of a haunted house attraction; those accounts have also not been verified.

Six Flags said it was “deeply saddened by the guest incident” and that it was supporting guests and staff affected.

Lisa Cupid, chairwoman of the Cobb County board of commissioners, said she “cannot imagine the horror the patrons and employees witnessed today”.

The Goliath rollercoaster opened in 2006 and reaches 70mph (113km/h) at a height of 200 feet (61 metres), according to the company’s website.

This marks at least the seventh death at the park, according to the Doan Law Firm, which tracks amusement park accidents. Earlier, one occurred on Goliath in 2006, after a man likely had a heart attack on the ride.

About two weeks ago, Six Flags Magic Mountain in California announced it would retire its X2 rollercoaster after more than 100 people reportedly sustained brain injuries while riding it.

The company said the ride had passed safety tests, but it was closing it regardless because it’s just the “right thing to do”.
